chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, altogether from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

The pilgrim is of three types: a type who is emancipated from the Fire, and a type who emerges from his sins as if he were like the day his mother gave birth to him, and a type who is preserved regarding his family and his wealth, and this is the least that the pilgrim returns with.

key_terms.يَوْمَ وَلَدَتْهُ أُمُّهُ: the day his mother gave birth to him

ai.seo_question: What are the three levels of reward for a pilgrim in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via the chain of Hisham ibn al-Hakam, highlighting the graded spiritual efficacy of Hajj based on the pilgrim's sincerity and presence of heart. While the lowest tier ensures worldly protection, the ultimate goal is the complete erasure of sins, reflecting the Shia emphasis on Hajj as a transformative mechanism for spiritual renewal rather than merely a ritual obligation.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazan, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The pilgrim is upon three types – a type who is emancipated from the Fire, and a type who comes out from his sins as if he was like the day his mother gave birth to him, and a type who is Protected regarding his family and his wealth – and it is the lowest of what the pilgrim returns with’.
en.sarwar: 39. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Jabir who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Al-H’ajj (people who perform al-Hajj) are of three kinds.

The one with the best share is one all of whose sins, those of the past and those to come are forgiven, and Allah protects him against the torments in the grave. Next to this is one whose sins of the past are forgiven but he begins his good deeds for the rest of his life. After these two is one who receives safety for his own self, family and property.’”
